texts: good. the "typical days" restriction becomes a premise of a fireable per-day rule, and "several vessels" keeps its group with its "several" count phrase; "with mire-essence" lands in the means slot, the closest licensed role for a substance, so the essence is still tied to the filling.
good. "heavy-thread day" keeps its day genus, the generic routes to a fireable per-day rule, and "four vessels" comes through as a per-day group carrying an exact count of four.

good. the "thin days" restriction becomes a premise of a fireable rule with the vessel and the essence both attached; the one thing to know is that "one vessel" leaves no explicit count atom — a single vessel is minted per thin day, so the number is implicit rather than queryable the way the four-vessel line's count is.

bad: "heavily" is dropped — a degree adverb on a verb has no slot in the instruction set, so the parse records only that distillation runs from early autumn to Lantern-night and loses the intensity, which is the point of the line. Move the intensity onto the distillation itself, where it becomes an ordinary property: "Heavy distillation runs from early autumn to Lantern-night." The interval and the Lantern-night name both parse fine as they stand.

mixed: everything is recorded, but "through deep winter" comes out as a point-in-time stamp rather than a span, so the thinning is not marked as holding across the whole season. One word fixes it — "throughout" is one of the three words that map to the span relation: "The distillation yield thins throughout deep winter."
